---- MODULE W4Od8m1p1t3 ----
\* Course-registration terminals arranged in a token ring. Only the terminal
\* holding the ring token may touch the shared enrollment record, and a write is
\* accepted only while the reading it was based on is still current -- so a slow
\* holder that dawdles and lets the record move on cannot silently lose an update.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

NRing == 3
Ring == 0 .. NRing - 1
Cap == 3
Amounts == {1, 2}
NoStage == [base |-> 0, amt |-> 0, fresh |-> FALSE]
MaxCommits == 3

VARIABLES holder, seats, staged, committed

vars == <<holder, seats, staged, committed>>

RECURSIVE Total(_)
Total(s) == IF s = <<>> THEN 0 ELSE Head(s) + Total(Tail(s))

TypeOK ==
    /\ holder \in Ring
    /\ seats \in 0 .. Cap
    /\ staged \in [Ring -> [base : 0 .. Cap, amt : 0 .. 2, fresh : BOOLEAN]]
    /\ committed \in Seq(Amounts)

Init ==
    /\ holder = 0
    /\ seats = 0
    /\ staged = [n \in Ring |-> NoStage]
    /\ committed = <<>>

\* Pass the ring token onward; a slow holder simply relinquishes without acting.
Advance ==
    /\ holder' = (holder + 1) % NRing
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seats, staged, committed>>

\* The token holder reads the current record and stages a seat grant against it.
Stage(n) ==
    /\ holder = n
    /\ staged[n].amt = 0
    /\ \E a \in Amounts :
         staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![n] = [base |-> seats, amt |-> a, fresh |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, seats, committed>>

\* The holder writes its staged grant, but only while that stage is still current;
\* the write lands as an absolute value derived from the reading it was based on.
Commit(n) ==
    /\ holder = n
    /\ staged[n].amt > 0
    /\ staged[n].fresh
    /\ Len(committed) < MaxCommits
    /\ staged[n].base + staged[n].amt <= Cap
    /\ seats' = staged[n].base + staged[n].amt
    /\ committed' = Append(committed, staged[n].amt)
    /\ staged' = [m \in Ring |->
                    IF m = n THEN NoStage
                    ELSE [staged[m] EXCEPT !.fresh = FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED holder

\* A holder whose stage went stale re-reads the record before retrying its grant.
Refresh(n) ==
    /\ holder = n
    /\ staged[n].amt > 0
    /\ ~staged[n].fresh
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![n] = [base |-> seats, amt |-> staged[n].amt, fresh |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, seats, committed>>

Next ==
    \/ Advance
    \/ \E n \in Ring : Stage(n) \/ Commit(n) \/ Refresh(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: the shared record equals the sum of every committed grant.
NoLostUpdates == seats = Total(committed)
====
nl:
A university course-registration system runs three enrollment terminals arranged
in a ring. A single ring token circulates; only the terminal currently holding
the token may read or write the shared enrollment record for a course. When a
terminal receives the token it may relinquish it again immediately -- a terminal
can be slow but is never considered failed, so the token keeps moving even past a
terminal that does nothing. A holder reads the current seat count and stages a
grant of one or two seats computed from that reading. It then commits the grant,
which writes the new seat count back as an absolute value derived from the reading
-- but the commit is allowed only while the stage is still current, that is, no
other commit has landed since the terminal read. Whenever any terminal commits,
every other terminal's outstanding stage is marked stale; a holder whose stage has
gone stale must re-read the record and refresh its stage before it may retry. Grants
never push enrollment past the course capacity.

Actions: pass the ring token to the next terminal; stage a one-or-two-seat grant
from the current reading; commit a still-current stage as an absolute write and
mark all other stages stale; refresh a stale stage by re-reading the record.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared enrollment count always equals the sum of every seat
grant that has been committed, so no committed update is ever lost by a stale write.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m9p6t1 ----
\* A runway allocator reconfigures itself in numbered epochs. Each epoch fixes the
\* set of controllers authorized to be granted a runway. Requests carry the epoch
\* they were issued under and may sit in the inbox and be delivered out of order, so
\* a request from a bygone epoch can surface after a reconfiguration; such a stale
\* request must never result in a grant, and a reconfiguration that drops a holder
\* must revoke that holder's runway.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

Parts == {0, 1, 2}
MaxEpoch == 2
MaxLog == 3
Free == [held |-> FALSE, by |-> 0, ep |-> 0]

VARIABLES epoch, authorized, inbox, runway, log

vars == <<epoch, authorized, inbox, runway, log>>

Reqs == [by : Parts, ep : 0 .. MaxEpoch]

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ authorized \in SUBSET Parts
    /\ inbox \in SUBSET Reqs
    /\ runway \in [held : BOOLEAN, by : Parts, ep : 0 .. MaxEpoch]
    /\ log \in Seq(Parts)

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ authorized = Parts
    /\ inbox = {}
    /\ runway = Free
    /\ log = <<>>

\* A controller issues a request stamped with the epoch it believes is current.
Request(p) ==
    /\ [by |-> p, ep |-> epoch] \notin inbox
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[by |-> p, ep |-> epoch]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, authorized, runway, log>>

\* A request is honoured only if it is for the current epoch and its issuer is still
\* authorized; the runway must be free. Out-of-order and stale requests fall through.
Grant(r) ==
    /\ r \in inbox
    /\ r.ep = epoch
    /\ r.by \in authorized
    /\ ~runway.held
    /\ Len(log) < MaxLog
    /\ runway' = [held |-> TRUE, by |-> r.by, ep |-> epoch]
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {r}
    /\ log' = Append(log, r.by)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, authorized>>

\* The current holder releases the runway.
Release ==
    /\ runway.held
    /\ runway' = Free
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, authorized, inbox, log>>

\* Reconfiguration advances to the next epoch number (cycling through a bounded band
\* of epoch labels), installs a fresh authorized set, and revokes the runway if its
\* holder is no longer authorized under the new configuration.
Reconfigure(S) ==
    /\ epoch' = (epoch + 1) % (MaxEpoch + 1)
    /\ authorized' = S
    /\ runway' = IF runway.held /\ runway.by \notin S THEN Free ELSE runway
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inbox, log>>

\* Housekeeping: discard a request whose epoch has already passed.
DropStale(r) ==
    /\ r \in inbox
    /\ r.ep < epoch
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, authorized, runway, log>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Parts : Request(p)
    \/ \E r \in inbox : Grant(r) \/ DropStale(r)
    \/ Release
    \/ \E S \in SUBSET Parts : Reconfigure(S)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Whoever holds the runway is authorized under the configuration in force right now.
OnlyAuthorizedHolds == ~runway.held \/ runway.by \in authorized
====
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator reconfigures itself in numbered epochs. Each epoch
fixes a set of controllers that are authorized to be granted a runway. A controller
issues a request stamped with the epoch it believes is current; requests accumulate
in an inbox and may be delivered out of order, so a request issued under an old epoch
can surface only after the system has already reconfigured. The allocator grants the
single runway to a request only when that request names the current epoch, its issuer
is in the current authorized set, and the runway is free. The holder later releases
the runway. A reconfiguration advances to the next epoch label (cycling through a
bounded band of epoch numbers), installs a fresh authorized set, and -- crucially --
revokes the runway immediately if the current holder is no longer in the new
authorized set. Stale requests left in the inbox may be discarded by housekeeping.

Actions: issue an epoch-stamped request; grant the runway to a current, authorized
request while it is free; release the runway; reconfigure to a new epoch and authorized
set, revoking the runway from a no-longer-authorized holder; drop a stale request.

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the runway is held, its holder is a controller authorized under
the epoch configuration currently in force, so no stale or unauthorized controller ever
holds the runway.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od8m9p1t0 ----
\* A course-registration back end keeps a single enrollment record carrying its own
\* generation stamp. Registrars update it with a compare-and-set on that stamp: an
\* update is staged against the generation the registrar last saw and lands only if
\* the record is still on that generation. The active registrar set is reconfigured
\* in numbered epochs, and one registrar may crash silently and stop participating.
\* Because a stale-generation write is refused, no committed update is ever lost.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

Parts == {0, 1, 2}
MaxGen == 3
MaxVal == 3
MaxH == 3
MaxEpoch == 2
NoStage == [rg |-> 0, nv |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]

VARIABLES epoch, active, record, history, crashed, staged

vars == <<epoch, active, record, history, crashed, staged>>

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ active = Parts
    /\ record = [val |-> 0, gen |-> 0]
    /\ history = <<>>
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ staged = [p \in Parts |-> NoStage]

\* An active, non-crashed registrar reads the record and stages the next enrollment,
\* remembering the generation it read.
Stage(p) ==
    /\ p \in active
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ ~staged[p].on
    /\ record.val < MaxVal
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![p] = [rg |-> record.gen, nv |-> record.val + 1, on |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, active, record, history, crashed>>

\* The staged write commits only if the record is still on the generation it read;
\* the record takes the new value and a generation one past the one read, and the
\* write is recorded in the history log.
Commit(p) ==
    /\ p \in active
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ staged[p].on
    /\ staged[p].rg = record.gen
    /\ Len(history) < MaxH
    /\ record' = [val |-> staged[p].nv, gen |-> staged[p].rg + 1]
    /\ history' = Append(history, p)
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![p] = NoStage]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, active, crashed>>

\* Reconfiguration advances the epoch label (cycling within a bounded band) and installs
\* a new active registrar set drawn from the registrars that have not crashed.
Reconfigure(S) ==
    /\ S \subseteq (Parts \ crashed)
    /\ epoch' = (epoch + 1) % (MaxEpoch + 1)
    /\ active' = S
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, history, crashed, staged>>

\* At most one registrar may crash silently; it stops staging and committing.
Crash(p) ==
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ p \in Parts
    /\ crashed' = {p}
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![p] = NoStage]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, active, record, history>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Parts : Stage(p) \/ Commit(p) \/ Crash(p)
    \/ \E S \in SUBSET Parts : Reconfigure(S)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: the record's advertised generation equals the number of updates
\* that actually landed in the history log.
NoLostUpdate == record.gen = Len(history)
====
nl:
A university course-registration system stores a single enrollment record that
carries its own generation stamp. Registrars update the record with a compare-and-set
on that stamp: a registrar first reads the record and stages the next enrollment,
remembering the generation number it saw; the staged write then commits only if the
record is still on exactly that generation, in which case the record takes the new
value and a generation one greater than the one read, and the write is appended to a
history log. The set of active registrars is reconfigured in numbered epochs (the
epoch label cycles through a bounded band), always drawing the new active set from
registrars that have not crashed. At most one registrar may crash silently, after
which it stops staging and committing altogether.

Actions: an active non-crashed registrar stages the next enrollment against the
generation it reads; it commits the staged write only when the record is still on that
generation, advancing the generation and recording the write in the history log;
reconfigure the active registrar set into the next epoch; crash one registrar silently.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the enrollment record's advertised generation always equals the number
of updates recorded in the history log, so a stale-generation write can never overwrite
and lose a committed update.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m4p5t2 ----
\* Two independent runway-allocation instances draw clearances from one shared, bounded
\* ready pool. Admission applies backpressure: no clearance is admitted while the pool is
\* full. Either instance may grab a clearance from the shared pool, and both can grab the
\* same one -- but firing a clearance (an irreversible go-around order) is guarded so it
\* happens at most once, even across the two instances racing on the same clearance.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

Jobs == {0, 1, 2}
Inst == {"A", "B"}
NONE == 9
Cap == 2
MaxFire == 3

VARIABLES admitted, hold, fired, fireLog, turn

vars == <<admitted, hold, fired, fireLog, turn>>

Init ==
    /\ admitted = {}
    /\ hold = [i \in Inst |-> NONE]
    /\ fired = {}
    /\ fireLog = <<>>
    /\ turn = "A"

\* Backpressure: a fresh clearance enters the shared pool only while it is not full.
Admit(j) ==
    /\ j \notin admitted
    /\ j \notin fired
    /\ Cardinality(admitted) < Cap
    /\ admitted' = admitted \cup {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, fired, fireLog, turn>>

\* An instance grabs a clearance from the shared pool; grabbing does not remove it, so
\* both instances can end up holding the same clearance.
Grab(i, j) ==
    /\ hold[i] = NONE
    /\ j \in admitted
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![i] = j]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<admitted, fired, fireLog, turn>>

\* Firing is the irreversible act; it is allowed only if this clearance has not already
\* been fired, so the two instances cannot both fire the one they share.
Fire(i) ==
    /\ hold[i] # NONE
    /\ hold[i] \notin fired
    /\ Len(fireLog) < MaxFire
    /\ fired' = fired \cup {hold[i]}
    /\ fireLog' = Append(fireLog, hold[i])
    /\ admitted' = admitted \ {hold[i]}
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![i] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED turn

\* An instance releases a clearance that a rival already fired.
Drop(i) ==
    /\ hold[i] # NONE
    /\ hold[i] \in fired
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![i] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<admitted, fired, fireLog, turn>>

\* The two instances poll the shared pool in alternation; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ turn' = IF turn = "A" THEN "B" ELSE "A"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<admitted, hold, fired, fireLog>>

Next ==
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Admit(j)
    \/ \E i \in Inst, j \in Jobs : Grab(i, j)
    \/ \E i \in Inst : Fire(i) \/ Drop(i)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* At most once: the fire log has exactly as many entries as there are distinct fired
\* clearances, so no clearance was ever fired twice.
FiredAtMostOnce == Len(fireLog) = Cardinality(fired)
====
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator runs two independent allocation instances that draw
clearances from one shared, bounded ready pool. Admission applies backpressure: a fresh
clearance is admitted into the pool only while the pool is below its capacity, so a full
pool blocks new admissions. Either instance may grab a clearance from the shared pool,
and grabbing does not remove it from the pool, so both instances can end up holding the
same clearance at once. Firing a clearance is the irreversible act -- it issues a
go-around order that cannot be recalled -- and it is guarded so that a clearance already
fired cannot be fired again, which keeps the two instances from both firing the clearance
they share. An instance that finds its held clearance was already fired by the rival
simply drops it. The two instances also poll the shared pool in strict alternation.

Actions: admit a fresh clearance under backpressure; an instance grabs a clearance from
the shared pool without removing it; fire a not-yet-fired held clearance irreversibly,
logging it and removing it from the pool; drop a held clearance a rival already fired;
alternate the polling turn between the two instances.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the fire log always has exactly as many entries as there are distinct
fired clearances, so no irreversible go-around order is ever issued twice for the same
clearance.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od0m3p6t3 ----
\* An operating-room scheduler elects a leader by term, with failover to a fresh leader
\* on a higher term. Only a leader that knows the current term may append a scheduling
\* decision, and every decision is stamped with the term it was made under. A newly
\* elected leader starts stale and must sync to the current term before scheduling; a
\* slow participant lags behind but is never failed. If a stale leader were allowed to
\* schedule, it would stamp a decision with a bygone term out of order.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

Parts == {0, 1, 2}
MaxTerm == 3
MaxLog == 3

VARIABLES term, leader, believed, log, hb

vars == <<term, leader, believed, log, hb>>

Monotone(s) == \A i \in 1 .. Len(s) - 1 : s[i] <= s[i + 1]

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerm
    /\ leader \in Parts
    /\ believed \in [Parts -> 0 .. MaxTerm]
    /\ log \in Seq(0 .. MaxTerm)
    /\ hb \in 0 .. 1

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = 0
    /\ believed = [p \in Parts |-> 0]
    /\ log = <<>>
    /\ hb = 0

\* Failover: raise the term and install a fresh leader, who starts out stale.
Elect(p) ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = p
    /\ UNCHANGED <<believed, log, hb>>

\* A slow participant catches up to the current term.
Sync(p) ==
    /\ believed[p] # term
    /\ believed' = [believed EXCEPT ![p] = term]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, log, hb>>

\* The leader appends a scheduling decision, but only while it knows the current term;
\* the decision is stamped with the term the leader believes it is.
Schedule ==
    /\ believed[leader] = term
    /\ Len(log) < MaxLog
    /\ log' = Append(log, believed[leader])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, believed, hb>>

\* A slow non-leader participant falls further behind, forgetting the term it knew.
Lag(p) ==
    /\ p # leader
    /\ believed[p] > 0
    /\ believed' = [believed EXCEPT ![p] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, log, hb>>

\* Heartbeats keep ticking whether or not anyone is scheduling; always available.
Heartbeat ==
    /\ hb' = (hb + 1) % 2
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, believed, log>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Parts : Elect(p) \/ Sync(p) \/ Lag(p)
    \/ Schedule
    \/ Heartbeat

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No stale action recorded: decision terms in the schedule log never decrease, so no
\* decision stamped by a leader lagging behind the current term is ever appended.
NoStaleDecision == Monotone(log)
====
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler elects a leader by term number, failing over to a
fresh leader on a strictly higher term. Only a leader that already knows the current
term may append a scheduling decision, and every decision it appends is stamped with the
term the leader believes it is operating under. A newly elected leader begins stale: it
does not yet know the raised term and must sync up to the current term before it is
allowed to schedule. Any participant may be slow -- lagging behind the current term --
but is never treated as failed, and heartbeats keep ticking regardless. Were a stale
leader permitted to schedule, it would stamp a decision with a bygone term and append it
after decisions already stamped with newer terms.

Actions: fail over by electing a fresh leader on the next term; sync a slow participant up
to the current term; let a slow non-leader participant fall further behind, forgetting the
term it knew; the leader appends a decision stamped with its believed term, but only while
that belief matches the current term and the log is not full; tick a heartbeat.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the term stamps recorded in the schedule log never decrease from one
decision to the next, so no stale leader lagging behind the current term ever gets a
decision into the log.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m6p2t5 ----
\* A runway allocator hands out a fixed pool of departure slots under time-limited
\* leases. A controller acquires free slots under a lease with an expiry deadline,
\* renews before expiry, or loses them back to the free pool once the lease expires.
\* A privileged admin can override, moving slots directly from one controller to
\* another. Slots are never created or destroyed: every slot is either free or held.
EXTENDS Naturals

Owners == {0, 1, 2}
Pool == 3
TTL == 2
MaxT == 2

VARIABLES free, held, lease, clock

vars == <<free, held, lease, clock>>

Sum == held[0] + held[1] + held[2]

TypeOK ==
    /\ free \in 0 .. Pool
    /\ held \in [Owners -> 0 .. Pool]
    /\ lease \in [Owners -> 0 .. TTL + MaxT]
    /\ clock \in 0 .. MaxT

Init ==
    /\ free = Pool
    /\ held = [o \in Owners |-> 0]
    /\ lease = [o \in Owners |-> 0]
    /\ clock = 0

\* Acquire some free slots under a fresh lease expiring TTL ticks from now.
Acquire(o, k) ==
    /\ k > 0
    /\ k <= free
    /\ free' = free - k
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![o] = held[o] + k]
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![o] = clock + TTL]
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

\* Renew the lease of a controller that still holds slots.
Renew(o) ==
    /\ held[o] > 0
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![o] = clock + TTL]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, held, clock>>

\* An expired lease returns all of that controller's slots to the free pool.
Expire(o) ==
    /\ held[o] > 0
    /\ clock >= lease[o]
    /\ free' = free + held[o]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![o] = 0]
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![o] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

\* Admin override: move k slots directly from one controller to another under a new lease.
Override(o1, o2, k) ==
    /\ o1 # o2
    /\ k > 0
    /\ k <= held[o1]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![o1] = held[o1] - k, ![o2] = held[o2] + k]
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![o2] = clock + TTL]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, clock>>

\* The lease clock advances, cycling within a bounded band; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ clock' = (clock + 1) % (MaxT + 1)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, held, lease>>

Next ==
    \/ \E o \in Owners, k \in 1 .. Pool : Acquire(o, k)
    \/ \E o \in Owners : Renew(o) \/ Expire(o)
    \/ \E o1 \in Owners, o2 \in Owners, k \in 1 .. Pool : Override(o1, o2, k)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Conservation: the free slots plus all held slots always total the fixed pool size.
Conserved == free + Sum = Pool
====
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator distributes a fixed pool of departure slots to
controllers under time-limited leases. A controller acquires one or more currently free
slots under a lease that expires a fixed number of ticks in the future; it may renew the
lease while it still holds slots; and once a lease has expired, all of that controller's
slots return to the free pool. A privileged admin can override the normal flow, moving
some slots directly from one controller to another and placing them under a fresh lease
for the recipient. The lease clock advances continuously, cycling within a bounded band
of tick values. At no point are slots created or destroyed -- every slot is at all times
either sitting in the free pool or held by exactly one controller.

Actions: acquire free slots under a fresh lease; renew a held lease; expire a lease,
returning its slots to the free pool; admin-override by moving slots from one controller
to another under a new lease; advance the lease clock.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of free slots plus the total number of slots held by all
controllers always equals the fixed pool size, so slots are never created or destroyed.

---- MODULE W4Od13m7p2t2 ----
\* Two dispenser instances in a vending-machine network share one coin vault exposed as a
\* compare-and-swap register. To dispense, an instance reads the vault, stages a swap to
\* the read-value-minus-one, and commits only if the vault is still on the value it read.
\* The committed value is written absolutely from the reading. Coins are conserved: every
\* coin is either still in the vault or counted as dispensed. If the swap ignored the read
\* value, a stale write would resurrect coins and break conservation.
EXTENDS Naturals

Inst == {"A", "B"}
Total == 3

VARIABLES vault, dispensed, attempt, turn

vars == <<vault, dispensed, attempt, turn>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ vault \in 0 .. Total
    /\ dispensed \in 0 .. Total
    /\ attempt \in [Inst -> [exp : 0 .. Total, on : BOOLEAN]]
    /\ turn \in Inst

Init ==
    /\ vault = Total
    /\ dispensed = 0
    /\ attempt = [i \in Inst |-> [exp |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ turn = "A"

\* An instance reads the shared vault and stages a swap based on that reading.
Stage(i) ==
    /\ ~attempt[i].on
    /\ vault > 0
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![i] = [exp |-> vault, on |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, dispensed, turn>>

\* Commit the swap only if the vault is still on the read value; the vault takes the
\* read value minus one (an absolute write) and a coin is counted as dispensed.
Commit(i) ==
    /\ attempt[i].on
    /\ attempt[i].exp = vault
    /\ vault > 0
    /\ vault' = attempt[i].exp - 1
    /\ dispensed' = dispensed + 1
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![i] = [exp |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED turn

\* An instance whose staged swap no longer matches the vault abandons it.
Abort(i) ==
    /\ attempt[i].on
    /\ attempt[i].exp # vault
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![i] = [exp |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, dispensed, turn>>

\* The two instances take turns polling the shared vault; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ turn' = IF turn = "A" THEN "B" ELSE "A"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, dispensed, attempt>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Inst : Stage(i) \/ Commit(i) \/ Abort(i)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Conservation: coins still in the vault plus coins dispensed always total the original.
CoinsConserved == vault + dispensed = Total
====
nl:
A vending-machine network runs two independent dispenser instances that share one coin
vault, which is exposed as a single compare-and-swap register. To dispense a coin, an
instance first reads the current vault balance and stages a swap to the value it read
minus one. It then commits the swap, but the commit succeeds only if the vault is still
sitting on exactly the value the instance read; when it succeeds, the vault is written
absolutely to that read value minus one and one more coin is counted as dispensed. An
instance whose staged swap no longer matches the current vault balance abandons the swap.
The two instances take turns polling the shared vault. No coin is ever created or
destroyed: every coin is either still resting in the vault or already counted as dispensed.

---- MODULE W4Od9m2p5t5 ----
\* A power-grid load shedder commits shed decisions by two-phase commit. A load is
\* proposed, participants vote, and once all have voted yes the coordinator commits and
\* "arms" the load -- charging a one-shot capacitor. Shedding the load is the irreversible
\* act: it fires the capacitor, discharging it and marking the load shed. Because the
\* capacitor is spent when it fires, a load can be shed at most once. A privileged admin
\* may override a load still in voting, aborting it back to idle.
EXTENDS Naturals

Loads == {0, 1}
Parts == {0, 1}

VARIABLES phase, yes, armed, done, hb

vars == <<phase, yes, armed, done, hb>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in [Loads -> {"idle", "voting", "commit"}]
    /\ yes \in [Loads -> SUBSET Parts]
    /\ armed \in [Loads -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ done \in SUBSET Loads
    /\ hb \in 0 .. 1

Init ==
    /\ phase = [l \in Loads |-> "idle"]
    /\ yes = [l \in Loads |-> {}]
    /\ armed = [l \in Loads |-> FALSE]
    /\ done = {}
    /\ hb = 0

\* Open a two-phase commit round for an idle load.
Propose(l) ==
    /\ phase[l] = "idle"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![l] = "voting"]
    /\ yes' = [yes EXCEPT ![l] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<armed, done, hb>>

\* A participant votes yes on a load under vote.
Vote(l, p) ==
    /\ phase[l] = "voting"
    /\ p \notin yes[l]
    /\ yes' = [yes EXCEPT ![l] = yes[l] \cup {p}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, armed, done, hb>>

\* All voted yes: commit and arm the load's one-shot capacitor.
Commit(l) ==
    /\ phase[l] = "voting"
    /\ yes[l] = Parts
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![l] = "commit"]
    /\ armed' = [armed EXCEPT ![l] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yes, done, hb>>

\* The irreversible shed: fire and discharge the capacitor, marking the load shed.
Shed(l) ==
    /\ armed[l]
    /\ l \notin done
    /\ armed' = [armed EXCEPT ![l] = FALSE]
    /\ done' = done \cup {l}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, yes, hb>>

\* Admin override: abort a load still under vote back to idle.
Override(l) ==
    /\ phase[l] = "voting"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![l] = "idle"]
    /\ yes' = [yes EXCEPT ![l] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<armed, done, hb>>

\* Grid heartbeat; always available.
Beat ==
    /\ hb' = (hb + 1) % 2
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, yes, armed, done>>

Next ==
    \/ \E l \in Loads : Propose(l) \/ Commit(l) \/ Shed(l) \/ Override(l)
    \/ \E l \in Loads, p \in Parts : Vote(l, p)
    \/ Beat

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* At most once: a load that has been shed has a spent capacitor, so it cannot fire again.
ShedOnce == \A l \in Loads : l \in done => ~armed[l]

participant may cast a yes vote. Once every participant has voted yes, the coordinator
commits the round and arms the load -- charging a one-shot capacitor for it. Shedding the

as shed. Because firing spends the capacitor, and a shed load is recorded so it is never
armed again, a load can be shed at most once. A privileged admin may override a load that
is still under vote, aborting it back to idle. A grid heartbeat ticks throughout.

fully-approved load and arm its capacitor; irreversibly shed an armed load, discharging the
capacitor and recording the load as shed; admin-override a voting load back to idle; tick
the heartbeat.

SAFETY PROPERTY: any load that has been shed has a discharged capacitor, so no load's
irreversible shed can ever fire a second time.

\* A warehouse robot fleet coordinates with two-level hierarchical locks: a coarse lock
\* per aisle (zone) and a fine lock per bin (cell). A robot may take a bin's fine lock only
\* while it already holds the coarse lock of the aisle that bin lives in, and it may operate
\* on a bin only while it holds both. A robot cannot drop an aisle's coarse lock while it
\* still holds any bin lock inside it. A privileged admin may override, clearing an aisle's
\* coarse lock together with every bin lock inside it at once.
EXTENDS Naturals

Zones == {0, 1}
Cells == {0, 1, 2, 3}
Robots == {0, 1}
FREE == 9
ZoneOf(c) == c \div 2

VARIABLES coarse, fine, work, turn

vars == <<coarse, fine, work, turn>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in [Zones -> Robots \cup {FREE}]
    /\ fine \in [Cells -> Robots \cup {FREE}]
    /\ work \in SUBSET Cells
    /\ turn \in Robots

Init ==
    /\ coarse = [z \in Zones |-> FREE]
    /\ fine = [c \in Cells |-> FREE]
    /\ work = {}
    /\ turn = 0

\* Take a free aisle coarse lock.
AcquireCoarse(z, r) ==
    /\ coarse[z] = FREE
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![z] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, work, turn>>

\* Take a bin fine lock, but only while holding the enclosing aisle's coarse lock.
AcquireFine(c, r) ==
    /\ coarse[ZoneOf(c)] = r
    /\ fine[c] = FREE
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![c] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, work, turn>>

\* Operate on a bin, allowed only while holding both its coarse and fine locks.
Operate(c, r) ==
    /\ fine[c] = r
    /\ coarse[ZoneOf(c)] = r
    /\ work' = work \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, turn>>

\* Release a bin fine lock.
ReleaseFine(c, r) ==
    /\ fine[c] = r
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![c] = FREE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, work, turn>>

\* Release an aisle coarse lock, only once no bin inside it is still locked by this robot.
ReleaseCoarse(z, r) ==
    /\ coarse[z] = r
    /\ \A c \in Cells : ZoneOf(c) = z => fine[c] # r
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![z] = FREE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, work, turn>>

\* Admin override: clear an aisle's coarse lock and every bin lock inside it together.
Override(z) ==
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![z] = FREE]
    /\ fine' = [c \in Cells |-> IF ZoneOf(c) = z THEN FREE ELSE fine[c]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<work, turn>>

\* Round-robin scheduling pulse; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ turn' = IF turn = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, work>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots, z \in Zones : AcquireCoarse(z, r) \/ ReleaseCoarse(z, r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, c \in Cells : AcquireFine(c, r) \/ Operate(c, r) \/ ReleaseFine(c, r)
    \/ \E z \in Zones : Override(z)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No unauthorized action: whoever holds a bin's fine lock also holds the coarse lock of
\* the aisle that bin belongs to, so no robot operates on a bin it is not authorized for.
LockHierarchy == \A c \in Cells : fine[c] # FREE => coarse[ZoneOf(c)] = fine[c]

A warehouse robot fleet coordinates access with two levels of hierarchical locks: a coarse
lock for each aisle and a fine lock for each individual bin, where every bin belongs to

---- MODULE W4Od15m8p1t5 ----
\* A stock-exchange opening auction protects its shared fill total with hierarchical locks:
\* a coarse lock over the whole book, and a fine lock per price level inside it. A trader
\* stages a fill by reading the current total under its locks, then commits by writing the
\* read value plus its size back absolutely. Because a commit demands both the book lock and
\* the price-level lock, no two fills race, and the recorded total never loses an update.
\* A privileged admin may override, releasing every lock at once.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

Prices == {0, 1}
Traders == {0, 1}
FREE == 9
MaxFills == 3

VARIABLES bookLock, priceLock, total, ledger, pend

vars == <<bookLock, priceLock, total, ledger, pend>>

RECURSIVE SumDeltas(_)
SumDeltas(s) == IF s = <<>> THEN 0 ELSE Head(s) + SumDeltas(Tail(s))

Init ==
    /\ bookLock = FREE
    /\ priceLock = [p \in Prices |-> FREE]
    /\ total = 0
    /\ ledger = <<>>
    /\ pend = [t \in Traders |-> [base |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]

\* Take the coarse book lock.
GrabBook(t) ==
    /\ bookLock = FREE
    /\ bookLock' = t
    /\ UNCHANGED <<priceLock, total, ledger, pend>>

\* Take a price-level fine lock, only while holding the book lock.
GrabPrice(p, t) ==
    /\ bookLock = t
    /\ priceLock[p] = FREE
    /\ priceLock' = [priceLock EXCEPT ![p] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bookLock, total, ledger, pend>>

\* Under both locks, read the current total and stage a one-lot fill against it.
Stage(p, t) ==
    /\ bookLock = t
    /\ priceLock[p] = t
    /\ ~pend[t].on
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![t] = [base |-> total, on |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bookLock, priceLock, total, ledger>>

\* Commit the staged fill: write the read value plus one back absolutely and log the lot.
Commit(t) ==
    /\ pend[t].on
    /\ bookLock = t
    /\ Len(ledger) < MaxFills
    /\ total' = pend[t].base + 1
    /\ ledger' = Append(ledger, 1)
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![t] = [base |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bookLock, priceLock>>

\* Release a price-level lock.
DropPrice(p, t) ==
    /\ priceLock[p] = t
    /\ priceLock' = [priceLock EXCEPT ![p] = FREE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bookLock, total, ledger, pend>>

\* Admin override: release the book lock and every price lock, and clear staged fills.
Override ==
    /\ bookLock' = FREE
    /\ priceLock' = [p \in Prices |-> FREE]
    /\ pend' = [t \in Traders |-> [base |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<total, ledger>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Traders : GrabBook(t) \/ Commit(t)
    \/ \E p \in Prices, t \in Traders : GrabPrice(p, t) \/ Stage(p, t) \/ DropPrice(p, t)
    \/ Override

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: the recorded fill total equals the sum of every logged fill lot.
NoLostFill == total = SumDeltas(ledger)
====

A stock-exchange opening auction protects its shared fill total with two levels of
hierarchical locks: a coarse lock over the whole order book, and a fine lock for each price
level inside it. A trader first takes the coarse book lock, then a price-level fine lock

fill against that reading. It then commits the fill by writing the value it read plus one
back to the total absolutely, appending the lot to the fill ledger. Because a commit demands
the book lock, fills cannot race one another, so the recorded total never loses an update. A
trader releases a price-level lock when done, and a privileged admin may override the whole
scheme, releasing the book lock and every price lock and clearing any staged fills at once.

Actions: grab the coarse book lock; grab a price-level fine lock while holding the book lock;
stage a one-lot fill by reading the total under both locks; commit the staged fill, writing

admin-override by releasing all locks and clearing staged fills.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the recorded fill total always equals the sum of every lot in the fill
ledger, so no committed fill is ever lost by a stale write.

\* voting. A surgeon requests the theatre, collects yes-votes from the staff, and may enter

\* holds the theatre. On exit the theatre and its backing clear. Because entry demands a

NONE == 9

Override ==

    /\ UNCHANGED turn

Tick ==
    /\ turn' = 1 - turn

    \/ Enter

    \/ Tick

---- MODULE W4Od8m2p2t1 ----
\* A course-registration system enrolls seats through two-phase commit. Each transaction
\* reserves one seat from the available pool on prepare, then either commits it into the
\* enrolled count or aborts it back to available. Decision messages can be delivered out of
\* order and even redundantly, so commits and aborts of prepared transactions may interleave
\* arbitrarily; guards make a duplicate decision a no-op. A finished transaction slot may be
\* reset for reuse. Throughout, seats are conserved: none are created or destroyed.
EXTENDS Naturals

TX == {0, 1, 2}
Total == 3

VARIABLES avail, reserved, enrolled, txState, clock

vars == <<avail, reserved, enrolled, txState, clock>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ avail \in 0 .. Total
    /\ reserved \in 0 .. Total
    /\ enrolled \in 0 .. Total
    /\ txState \in [TX -> {"none", "prepared", "committed", "aborted"}]
    /\ clock \in {0, 1}

Init ==
    /\ avail = Total
    /\ reserved = 0
    /\ enrolled = 0
    /\ txState = [t \in TX |-> "none"]
    /\ clock = 0

\* Prepare: reserve one available seat for a fresh transaction.
Prepare(t) ==
    /\ txState[t] = "none"
    /\ avail > 0
    /\ avail' = avail - 1
    /\ reserved' = reserved + 1
    /\ txState' = [txState EXCEPT ![t] = "prepared"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, clock>>

\* Commit: move a prepared transaction's reserved seat into the enrolled count.
Commit(t) ==
    /\ txState[t] = "prepared"
    /\ reserved' = reserved - 1
    /\ enrolled' = enrolled + 1
    /\ txState' = [txState EXCEPT ![t] = "committed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<avail, clock>>

\* Abort: return a prepared transaction's reserved seat to the available pool.
Abort(t) ==
    /\ txState[t] = "prepared"
    /\ reserved' = reserved - 1
    /\ avail' = avail + 1
    /\ txState' = [txState EXCEPT ![t] = "aborted"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, clock>>

\* Reset a finished transaction slot for reuse; seats are untouched.
Reset(t) ==
    /\ txState[t] \in {"committed", "aborted"}
    /\ txState' = [txState EXCEPT ![t] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<avail, reserved, enrolled, clock>>

\* Timing pulse standing in for message delivery; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ clock' = 1 - clock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<avail, reserved, enrolled, txState>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in TX : Prepare(t) \/ Commit(t) \/ Abort(t) \/ Reset(t)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Conservation: available, reserved, and enrolled seats always total the fixed capacity.
SeatsConserved == avail + reserved + enrolled = Total
====
nl:
A university course-registration system enrolls seats through two-phase commit. Each
transaction, on prepare, reserves exactly one seat from the available pool. It then either
commits -- moving that reserved seat into the enrolled count -- or aborts, returning the
reserved seat to the available pool. Decision messages can be delivered out of order and even
redundantly, so commits and aborts of the various prepared transactions may interleave in any
order; the state guards make a duplicate or late decision on an already-finished transaction a
no-op. A finished transaction slot (committed or aborted) may be reset so it can be reused for
a new transaction, without touching any seat counts. A timing pulse ticks throughout.

Actions: prepare a fresh transaction, reserving one available seat; commit a prepared
transaction, moving its seat to enrolled; abort a prepared transaction, returning its seat to
available; reset a finished transaction slot for reuse; tick the timing pulse.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the available seats plus the reserved seats plus the enrolled seats always
equal the fixed course capacity, so no seat is ever created or destroyed.

\* print token for it. Printing the ticket is the irreversible act: it consumes the token
\* via a compare-and-swap from armed to spent, so a ticket can be printed at most once. A
\* held seat may be cancelled only before its ticket is printed. The course capacity is not
\* fixed -- it may be resized at runtime -- and enrollment respects the current capacity.

Seats == {0, 1, 2}
MaxCap == 3

VARIABLES cap, token, printed, reg

vars == <<cap, token, printed, reg>>

Held == Cardinality({s \in Seats : reg[s] = "held"})

    /\ cap \in 0 .. MaxCap
    /\ token \in [Seats -> {0, 1}]
    /\ printed \in SUBSET Seats
    /\ reg \in [Seats -> {"empty", "held"}]

Init ==
    /\ cap = MaxCap
    /\ token = [s \in Seats |-> 0]
    /\ printed = {}
    /\ reg = [s \in Seats |-> "empty"]

Enroll(s) ==
    /\ reg[s] = "empty"
    /\ Held < cap
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![s] = "held"]
    /\ token' = [token EXCEPT ![s] = 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, printed>>

\* Print the ticket: compare-and-swap the token from armed to spent (irreversible).
Print(s) ==
    /\ token[s] = 1
    /\ s \notin printed
    /\ token' = [token EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
    /\ printed' = printed \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, reg>>

\* Cancel a held seat, but only before its ticket has been printed.
Cancel(s) ==
    /\ reg[s] = "held"
    /\ s \notin printed
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![s] = "empty"]
    /\ token' = [token EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, printed>>

\* Capacity changes at runtime to a different value; always available.
Resize(c) ==
    /\ c # cap
    /\ cap' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, printed, reg>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Seats : Enroll(s) \/ Print(s) \/ Cancel(s)
    \/ \E c \in 0 .. MaxCap : Resize(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* At most once: any seat whose ticket has been printed has a spent print token, so its
\* irreversible ticket print can never fire a second time.
PrintOnce == \A s \in Seats : s \in printed => token[s] = 0

only while the number of held seats is below the current capacity, and enrolling arms a
one-use print token for that seat. Printing the ticket is the irreversible act: it consumes

but only before its ticket has been printed; cancelling frees the seat and clears its token.

enrollment always respects whatever capacity is currently in force.

printed seat; resize the capacity at runtime to a different value.

SAFETY PROPERTY: any seat whose ticket has been printed has a spent print token, so the
irreversible act of printing an enrollment ticket can never fire a second time for that seat.

---- MODULE W4Od7m1p6t3 ----
\* A container-ship crane yard grants exclusive berth access with a single circulating
\* token. Only the crane currently holding the token may begin an operation, and the token
\* cannot be passed onward while its holder is still busy. A crane may be slow -- taking its
\* time on an operation -- but is never failed; the yard clock keeps ticking meanwhile. If a
\* non-holder could begin work, or the token slipped away from a busy crane, an unauthorized
\* crane would be operating.
EXTENDS Naturals

Cranes == {0, 1, 2}
N == 3
MaxOps == 3

VARIABLES token, busy, served, clock

vars == <<token, busy, served, clock>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Cranes
    /\ busy \in [Cranes -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ served \in 0 .. MaxOps
    /\ clock \in {0, 1}

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ busy = [c \in Cranes |-> FALSE]
    /\ served = 0
    /\ clock = 0

\* Only the token holder may begin an operation.
Begin(c) ==
    /\ c = token
    /\ ~busy[c]
    /\ busy' = [busy EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, served, clock>>

\* A busy crane finishes its operation.
Finish(c) ==
    /\ busy[c]
    /\ served < MaxOps
    /\ busy' = [busy EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ served' = served + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, clock>>

\* Pass the token to the next crane, but never while the current holder is busy.
Pass ==
    /\ ~busy[token]
    /\ token' = (token + 1) % N
    /\ UNCHANGED <<busy, served, clock>>

\* The yard clock ticks whether or not a crane is slow; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ clock' = 1 - clock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, busy, served>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Begin(c) \/ Finish(c)
    \/ Pass
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No unauthorized operation: any crane that is busy is the one holding the token.
OnlyHolderWorks == \A c \in Cranes : busy[c] => c = token
====
nl:
A container-ship crane yard grants exclusive berth access with a single token that
circulates among the cranes. Only the crane currently holding the token may begin an
operation. A busy crane eventually finishes its operation. The token may be passed onward to
the next crane, but never while the crane currently holding it is still busy. A crane may be
slow -- taking its time over an operation -- but it is never treated as failed, and the yard
clock keeps ticking regardless of how slow a crane is. Were a non-holder allowed to begin
work, or the token allowed to slip away from a crane that was still busy, an unauthorized
crane would end up operating a berth.

Actions: the token holder begins an operation; a busy crane finishes its operation; pass the
token to the next crane, but only while the current holder is not busy; tick the yard clock.

---- MODULE W4Od5m3p3t3 ----
\* A multiplayer lobby matchmaker elects a leader (with failover to a new leader on a fresh
\* term) that hands out per-slot leases to players. A slot can be allocated to a player only
\* while that player holds the slot's lease, and a lease is held by at most one player. A
\* player may be slow to claim a slot it has leased, but is never failed. Since a slot is
\* allocated only to its unique lease-holder, the same slot is never allocated to two players.
EXTENDS Naturals

Slots == {0, 1}
Players == {0, 1, 2}
NONE == 9
MaxTerm == 1

VARIABLES leader, leaseOf, allocOf, term

vars == <<leader, leaseOf, allocOf, term>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Players
    /\ leaseOf \in [Slots -> Players \cup {NONE}]
    /\ allocOf \in [Slots -> Players \cup {NONE}]
    /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerm

Init ==
    /\ leader = 0
    /\ leaseOf = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ allocOf = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ term = 0

\* Failover: bump the term (cycling within a bounded band) and install a fresh leader.
Elect(p) ==
    /\ term' = (term + 1) % (MaxTerm + 1)
    /\ leader' = p
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseOf, allocOf>>

\* The leader grants a free slot's lease to a player.
Lease(s, p) ==
    /\ leaseOf[s] = NONE
    /\ leaseOf' = [leaseOf EXCEPT ![s] = p]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, allocOf, term>>

\* A player allocates a slot, but only while it holds that slot's lease.
Allocate(s, p) ==
    /\ leaseOf[s] = p
    /\ allocOf[s] = NONE
    /\ allocOf' = [allocOf EXCEPT ![s] = p]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, leaseOf, term>>

\* Release a slot, clearing both its allocation and its lease.
Release(s) ==
    /\ allocOf[s] # NONE
    /\ allocOf' = [allocOf EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ leaseOf' = [leaseOf EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Players : Elect(p)
    \/ \E s \in Slots, p \in Players : Lease(s, p) \/ Allocate(s, p)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Release(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No double allocation: an allocated slot is allocated to its unique lease-holder, so it
\* cannot also be allocated to any other player.
NoDoubleAlloc == \A s \in Slots : allocOf[s] # NONE => allocOf[s] = leaseOf[s]
====
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker elects a leader that hands out per-slot leases to
players, failing over to a fresh leader on a new term. The leader grants a free slot's lease
to a player, and a slot can be allocated to a player only while that player currently holds
that slot's lease; a lease is held by at most one player at a time. A player may be slow to
claim a slot it has already leased -- nothing forces it to allocate promptly -- but it is
never treated as failed. Releasing a slot clears both its allocation and its lease. Because a
slot is only ever allocated to the single player holding its lease, the same slot can never be
allocated to two different players.

Actions: fail over by electing a fresh leader on the next term; the leader grants a free
slot's lease to a player; a player allocates a slot it holds the lease for; release a slot,
clearing its allocation and lease.

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a slot is allocated, it is allocated to the very player that holds
that slot's lease, so no slot is ever double-allocated to two players at once.

---- MODULE W4Od14m9p6t4 ----
\* A wildfire drone surveillance swarm reconfigures itself in numbered epochs. Each drone
\* carries a belief about the current epoch and may take a surveillance assignment only after
\* syncing that belief to the live epoch; the number of concurrently assigned drones is
\* capped by a capacity that itself changes at each reconfiguration. Reconfiguration advances
\* the epoch, resets the capacity, and stands down every assigned drone, which must re-sync
\* before assigning again. A drone lagging on an old epoch must not remain assigned.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Drones == {0, 1, 2}
MaxEpoch == 2
MaxCap == 3

VARIABLES epoch, capacity, belief, active

vars == <<epoch, capacity, belief, active>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ capacity \in 0 .. MaxCap
    /\ belief \in [Drones -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]
    /\ active \in SUBSET Drones

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ capacity = MaxCap
    /\ belief = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
    /\ active = {}

\* Reconfiguration advances the epoch, resets capacity, and stands down all assigned drones.
Reconfigure(c) ==
    /\ epoch' = (epoch + 1) % (MaxEpoch + 1)
    /\ capacity' = c
    /\ active' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED belief

\* A drone syncs its belief to the live epoch.
Sync(d) ==
    /\ belief[d] # epoch
    /\ belief' = [belief EXCEPT ![d] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity, active>>

\* A synced drone takes a surveillance assignment while capacity allows.
Assign(d) ==
    /\ belief[d] = epoch
    /\ d \notin active
    /\ Cardinality(active) < capacity
    /\ active' = active \cup {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity, belief>>

\* A drone stands down from its assignment.
Deassign(d) ==
    /\ d \in active
    /\ active' = active \ {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity, belief>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in 0 .. MaxCap : Reconfigure(c)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Sync(d) \/ Assign(d) \/ Deassign(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No stale action: every assigned drone believes the current epoch, so no drone lagging on
\* a bygone epoch is ever holding a live surveillance assignment.
NoStaleAssignment == \A d \in active : belief[d] = epoch
====
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm reconfigures itself in numbered epochs. Each drone
carries a belief about which epoch is current, and a drone may take a surveillance assignment
only after it has synced that belief up to the live epoch. The number of drones assigned at
once is capped by a capacity, and that capacity itself is reset at every reconfiguration.
Reconfiguration advances the epoch label (cycling within a bounded band), installs a new
capacity, and stands down every currently assigned drone, each of which must re-sync before it
can assign again. A drone lagging on a bygone epoch must never remain holding a live
assignment.

Actions: reconfigure -- advance the epoch, reset the capacity, and stand down all assigned
drones; sync a drone's belief to the live epoch; a synced drone takes an assignment while the
current capacity has room; a drone stands down from its assignment.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every drone that currently holds a surveillance assignment believes the live
epoch, so no drone lagging on a stale epoch is ever holding a live assignment.

---- MODULE W4Od9m6p2t5 ----
\* A power-grid load shedder keeps a fixed quantity of megawatts flowing among three books:
\* spinning reserve, dispatched-to-feeders, and curtailed (shed but still accounted for).
\* Megawatts are dispatched from spinning reserve to a feeder under a time-limited lease,
\* recalled to reserve when the lease expires, and -- under a privileged admin override --
\* curtailed from reserve or restored back to it. No megawatt is created or lost: the three
\* books always sum to the grid's fixed total.
EXTENDS Naturals

Feeders == {0, 1, 2}
Total == 3
TTL == 2
MaxT == 2

VARIABLES spinning, dispatched, curtailed, lease, clock

vars == <<spinning, dispatched, curtailed, lease, clock>>

Dispatched == dispatched[0] + dispatched[1] + dispatched[2]

TypeOK ==
    /\ spinning \in 0 .. Total
    /\ dispatched \in [Feeders -> 0 .. Total]
    /\ curtailed \in 0 .. Total
    /\ lease \in [Feeders -> 0 .. TTL + MaxT]
    /\ clock \in 0 .. MaxT

Init ==
    /\ spinning = Total
    /\ dispatched = [f \in Feeders |-> 0]
    /\ curtailed = 0
    /\ lease = [f \in Feeders |-> 0]
    /\ clock = 0

\* Dispatch megawatts from spinning reserve to a feeder under a fresh lease.
Dispatch(f, k) ==
    /\ k > 0
    /\ k <= spinning
    /\ spinning' = spinning - k
    /\ dispatched' = [dispatched EXCEPT ![f] = dispatched[f] + k]
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![f] = clock + TTL]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<curtailed, clock>>

\* Renew a feeder's dispatch lease.
Renew(f) ==
    /\ dispatched[f] > 0
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![f] = clock + TTL]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<spinning, dispatched, curtailed, clock>>

\* An expired lease recalls all of a feeder's megawatts to spinning reserve.
Recall(f) ==
    /\ dispatched[f] > 0
    /\ clock >= lease[f]
    /\ spinning' = spinning + dispatched[f]
    /\ dispatched' = [dispatched EXCEPT ![f] = 0]
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![f] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<curtailed, clock>>

\* Admin override: curtail megawatts out of spinning reserve into the curtailed book.
Curtail(k) ==
    /\ k > 0
    /\ k <= spinning
    /\ spinning' = spinning - k
    /\ curtailed' = curtailed + k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dispatched, lease, clock>>

\* Admin override: restore curtailed megawatts back to spinning reserve.
Restore(k) ==
    /\ k > 0
    /\ k <= curtailed
    /\ spinning' = spinning + k
    /\ curtailed' = curtailed - k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dispatched, lease, clock>>

\* The lease clock advances, cycling within a bounded band; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ clock' = (clock + 1) % (MaxT + 1)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<spinning, dispatched, curtailed, lease>>

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Feeders, k \in 1 .. Total : Dispatch(f, k)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : Renew(f) \/ Recall(f)
    \/ \E k \in 1 .. Total : Curtail(k) \/ Restore(k)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Conservation: spinning reserve, dispatched, and curtailed megawatts always sum to the total.
PowerConserved == spinning + Dispatched + curtailed = Total
====
nl:
A power-grid load shedder keeps a fixed quantity of megawatts flowing among three books:
spinning reserve, megawatts dispatched to feeders, and megawatts curtailed (shed but still
accounted for). Megawatts are dispatched from spinning reserve to a feeder under a
time-limited lease; a feeder's lease may be renewed while it carries load; and once a lease
expires, all of that feeder's megawatts are recalled to spinning reserve. Under a privileged
admin override, megawatts may be curtailed out of spinning reserve into the curtailed book,
or restored from the curtailed book back into spinning reserve. The lease clock advances
continuously, cycling within a bounded band. No megawatt is ever created or lost.

Actions: dispatch megawatts from reserve to a feeder under a fresh lease; renew a feeder's
lease; recall an expired feeder's megawatts to reserve; admin-curtail megawatts from reserve
into the curtailed book; admin-restore curtailed megawatts back to reserve; advance the clock.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the spinning reserve plus the megawatts dispatched to feeders plus the
megawatts curtailed always equal the grid's fixed total, so no megawatt is ever created or
destroyed.

---- MODULE W4Od2m0p1t5 ----
\* Warehouse robots update a shared inventory record using optimistic locking with retry.
\* A robot reads the record's current version, then commits a new version derived from the
\* one it read -- but only if the record is still on that version. If the record has moved on,
\* the robot must retry by re-reading. Each successful commit records the new version in a
\* version log. A privileged admin may override, clearing all outstanding optimistic attempts.
\* Under this discipline the version log advances one step at a time, losing no update.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

Robots == {0, 1}
MaxV == 3

VARIABLES version, vlog, pend, clock

vars == <<version, vlog, pend, clock>>

Contiguous(s) ==
    \/ Len(s) = 0
    \/ /\ s[1] = 1
       /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(s) - 1 : s[i + 1] = s[i] + 1

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in 0 .. MaxV
    /\ vlog \in Seq(1 .. MaxV)
    /\ pend \in [Robots -> [rv : 0 .. MaxV, on : BOOLEAN]]
    /\ clock \in {0, 1}

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ vlog = <<>>
    /\ pend = [r \in Robots |-> [rv |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ clock = 0

\* Read the record's current version optimistically.
Read(r) ==
    /\ ~pend[r].on
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![r] = [rv |-> version, on |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, vlog, clock>>

\* Commit a new version derived from the read, only if the record is still on that version.
Commit(r) ==
    /\ pend[r].on
    /\ pend[r].rv = version
    /\ Len(vlog) < MaxV
    /\ version' = pend[r].rv + 1
    /\ vlog' = Append(vlog, pend[r].rv + 1)
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![r] = [rv |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

\* The record moved on: retry by re-reading the current version.
Retry(r) ==
    /\ pend[r].on
    /\ pend[r].rv # version
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![r] = [rv |-> version, on |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, vlog, clock>>

\* Admin override: clear all outstanding optimistic attempts; always available.
Override ==
    /\ pend' = [r \in Robots |-> [rv |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, vlog, clock>>

\* Housekeeping pulse.
Tick ==
    /\ clock' = 1 - clock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, vlog, pend>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Read(r) \/ Commit(r) \/ Retry(r)
    \/ Override
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: committed versions form a gapless run 1, 2, 3, ..., so no stale commit
\* ever regresses or duplicates a version and loses an update.
NoLostUpdate == Contiguous(vlog)
====
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet updates a shared inventory record using optimistic locking with
retry. A robot first reads the record's current version number. It then commits a new version,
derived by adding one to the version it read, but the commit is accepted only if the record is
still sitting on exactly the version the robot read. If the record has already moved on, the
robot must retry: it re-reads the current version and tries again. Each accepted commit appends
the new version number to a version log. A privileged admin may override at any time, clearing
every outstanding optimistic attempt. A housekeeping pulse ticks throughout.

Actions: read the current version optimistically; commit a new version derived from the read
when the record is still on that version, logging the new version; retry by re-reading when the
record has moved on; admin-override to clear all outstanding attempts; tick the housekeeping pulse.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the committed version numbers in the log form a gapless run 1, 2, 3, and so on,
so no stale commit ever regresses or duplicates a version, and no update is ever lost.

---- MODULE W4Od6m3p1t4 ----
\* An elevator bank keeps a shared board of floor calls. A leader (elected, with failover to a
\* new term) posts calls onto the board up to a runtime-adjustable capacity, acknowledges calls
\* it commits to serve, and serves them -- removing served calls from both the board and the
\* acknowledged set. Unacknowledged calls may be pruned from the board, but an acknowledged call
\* must never be dropped from the board without being served. Thus no acknowledged call is lost.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Reqs == {0, 1, 2}
MaxCap == 3
MaxTerm == 1

VARIABLES board, acked, capacity, term

vars == <<board, acked, capacity, term>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ board \in SUBSET Reqs
    /\ acked \in SUBSET Reqs
    /\ capacity \in 0 .. MaxCap
    /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerm

Init ==
    /\ board = {}
    /\ acked = {}
    /\ capacity = MaxCap
    /\ term = 0

\* Post a new floor call onto the board while capacity allows.
Post(r) ==
    /\ r \notin board
    /\ Cardinality(board) < capacity
    /\ board' = board \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acked, capacity, term>>

\* Acknowledge a posted call, committing to serve it.
Ack(r) ==
    /\ r \in board
    /\ r \notin acked
    /\ acked' = acked \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<board, capacity, term>>

\* Serve an acknowledged call, removing it from both the board and the acknowledged set.
Serve(r) ==
    /\ r \in acked
    /\ board' = board \ {r}
    /\ acked' = acked \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, term>>

\* Prune an unacknowledged call from the board.
Prune(r) ==
    /\ r \in board
    /\ r \notin acked
    /\ board' = board \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acked, capacity, term>>

\* Failover: elect a fresh leader term (cycling within a bounded band).
Elect ==
    /\ term' = (term + 1) % (MaxTerm + 1)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<board, acked, capacity>>

\* Capacity changes at runtime to a different value; always available.
Resize(c) ==
    /\ c # capacity
    /\ capacity' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<board, acked, term>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Reqs : Post(r) \/ Ack(r) \/ Serve(r) \/ Prune(r)
    \/ Elect
    \/ \E c \in 0 .. MaxCap : Resize(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: every acknowledged floor call is still on the board, so no committed call
\* is ever silently dropped.
NoCallLost == acked \subseteq board
====
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper keeps a shared board of outstanding floor calls, coordinated
by an elected leader that fails over to a fresh term when needed. The leader posts new floor
calls onto the board, but only while the number of calls on the board is below a capacity that
can be adjusted at runtime. The leader acknowledges a posted call when it commits to serving
it, and later serves an acknowledged call, removing it from both the board and the
acknowledged set at once. A call that has not been acknowledged may be pruned from the board,
but an acknowledged call must never be dropped from the board except by serving it. As a
result, no call the system has committed to is ever lost.

Actions: post a new floor call while under capacity; acknowledge a posted call; serve an
acknowledged call, removing it from board and acknowledged set; prune an unacknowledged call
from the board; fail over to a fresh leader term; resize the board capacity at runtime.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every acknowledged floor call is always still present on the board, so no
call the elevator bank has committed to serve is ever silently lost.

---- MODULE W4Od7m5p4t0 ----
\* A container-ship crane yard admits cranes to operate only by quorum vote, and at most a
\* bounded number of cranes may be operating at once. A crane proposes to start, the others
\* vote, and it begins only with a strict majority and while the operating count is below the
\* bound. A crane later stops. One crane may crash silently while idle, after which it neither
\* proposes nor votes. The number of cranes operating at once never exceeds the bound.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Cranes == {0, 1, 2}
Capacity == 2
NONE == 9

VARIABLES operating, votes, pending, crashed, clock

vars == <<operating, votes, pending, crashed, clock>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ operating \in SUBSET Cranes
    /\ votes \in SUBSET Cranes
    /\ pending \in Cranes \cup {NONE}
    /\ crashed \in SUBSET Cranes
    /\ clock \in {0, 1}

Init ==
    /\ operating = {}
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ pending = NONE
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ clock = 0

\* A non-operating, non-crashed crane proposes to start, resetting the tally.
Propose(c) ==
    /\ pending = NONE
    /\ c \notin operating
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ pending' = c
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<operating, crashed, clock>>

\* A non-crashed crane votes yes on the pending proposal.
Vote(v) ==
    /\ pending # NONE
    /\ v \notin crashed
    /\ v \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {v}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<operating, pending, crashed, clock>>

\* The pending crane starts operating, only with a strict majority and room under the bound.
Start ==
    /\ pending # NONE
    /\ 2 * Cardinality(votes) > Cardinality(Cranes)
    /\ Cardinality(operating) < Capacity
    /\ operating' = operating \cup {pending}
    /\ pending' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, crashed, clock>>

\* An operating crane stops.
Stop(c) ==
    /\ c \in operating
    /\ operating' = operating \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, pending, crashed, clock>>

\* One idle crane may crash silently.
Crash(c) ==
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ c \notin operating
    /\ c # pending
    /\ crashed' = {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<operating, votes, pending, clock>>

\* Yard clock; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ clock' = 1 - clock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<operating, votes, pending, crashed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Propose(c) \/ Stop(c) \/ Crash(c)
    \/ \E v \in Cranes : Vote(v)
    \/ Start
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounded capacity: the number of cranes operating at once never exceeds the bound.
WithinCapacity == Cardinality(operating) <= Capacity
====
nl:
A container-ship crane yard admits cranes to operate only by quorum vote, and at most a bounded
number of cranes may be operating at once. A crane that is idle and not crashed proposes to
start, which resets the vote tally; the other non-crashed cranes then vote yes. The proposing
crane begins operating only when a strict majority has voted for it and the number of cranes
already operating is below the bound. An operating crane later stops. One crane may crash
silently while it is idle, after which it neither proposes nor votes. A yard clock ticks
throughout.

Actions: an idle non-crashed crane proposes to start, resetting the tally; a non-crashed crane
votes yes; the pending crane starts operating given a strict majority and room under the bound;
an operating crane stops; one idle crane crashes silently; tick the yard clock.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of cranes operating at once never exceeds the fixed bound.

---- MODULE W4Od18m3p6t1 ----
\* A smart-home door-lock network is driven by an elected hub. Nodes send lock/unlock commands
\* into a shared inbox; commands may be delivered out of order, and a deposed hub can still emit
\* a command that surfaces late. A command executes on the lock only if its sender is the hub
\* currently authorized; an election installs a fresh authorized hub and clears the record of who
\* last executed. Stale commands from a non-authorized sender must never take effect on the lock.
EXTENDS Naturals

Nodes == {0, 1, 2}
Ops == {"lock", "unlock"}
NONE == 9
MaxTerm == 1

VARIABLES term, granted, inbox, lock, execBy

vars == <<term, granted, inbox, lock, execBy>>

Cmds == [by : Nodes, op : Ops]

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerm
    /\ granted \in Nodes \cup {NONE}
    /\ inbox \in SUBSET Cmds
    /\ lock \in {"locked", "unlocked"}
    /\ execBy \in Nodes \cup {NONE}

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ granted = 0
    /\ inbox = {}
    /\ lock = "locked"
    /\ execBy = NONE

\* Elect a fresh authorized hub on the next term, clearing the last-executor record.
Elect(n) ==
    /\ term' = (term + 1) % (MaxTerm + 1)
    /\ granted' = n
    /\ execBy' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inbox, lock>>

\* Any node may send a command into the shared inbox (a deposed hub's command may linger).
Send(n, o) ==
    /\ [by |-> n, op |-> o] \notin inbox
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[by |-> n, op |-> o]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, granted, lock, execBy>>

\* A command executes on the lock only if its sender is the currently authorized hub.
Execute(c) ==
    /\ c \in inbox
    /\ c.by = granted
    /\ lock' = c.op
    /\ execBy' = c.by
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, granted>>

\* Discard a command whose sender is not the currently authorized hub.
DropStale(c) ==
    /\ c \in inbox
    /\ c.by # granted
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, granted, lock, execBy>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, o \in Ops : Send(n, o)
    \/ \E c \in inbox : Execute(c) \/ DropStale(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No stale action: whoever last executed a command on the lock is the currently authorized
\* hub, so no command from a deposed or unauthorized sender ever takes effect.
OnlyAuthorizedExec == execBy = NONE \/ execBy = granted
====
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network is driven by an elected hub. Nodes send lock and unlock
commands into a shared inbox, and those commands may be delivered out of order; in particular
a hub that has since been deposed can still have emitted a command that only surfaces later. A
command executes on the door lock only if its sender is the hub that is currently authorized. An
election installs a fresh authorized hub on a new term and clears the record of which node last
executed a command. A command whose sender is not the currently authorized hub is simply
discarded from the inbox. A stale command from a deposed or otherwise unauthorized sender must
never take effect on the lock.

Actions: elect a fresh authorized hub on the next term, clearing the last-executor record; any
node sends a lock/unlock command into the shared inbox; execute an inbox command whose sender is
the currently authorized hub, applying it to the lock; discard an inbox command from a
non-authorized sender.

SAFETY PROPERTY: whoever last executed a command on the door lock is the currently authorized
hub, so no command from a deposed or unauthorized sender ever takes effect.

---- MODULE W4Od15m1p5t5 ----
\* A stock-exchange opening auction runs one matching engine, accessed exclusively by whichever
\* trader holds the ring token. Each order lives in exactly one of three disjoint books: open,
\* matched, or printed. The token holder moves an open order to matched, then irreversibly prints
\* it -- moving it from matched to printed, which is terminal. Because printing requires the order
\* to be in the matched book and moves it out, an order is printed at most once. A privileged
\* admin may override a matched order back to open. The three books stay pairwise disjoint.
EXTENDS Naturals

Orders == {0, 1, 2}
Traders == {0, 1}

VARIABLES token, open, matched, printed

vars == <<token, open, matched, printed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Traders
    /\ open \in SUBSET Orders
    /\ matched \in SUBSET Orders
    /\ printed \in SUBSET Orders

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ open = {}
    /\ matched = {}
    /\ printed = {}

\* Pass the ring token to the next trader; always available.
Pass ==
    /\ token' = (token + 1) % 2
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, matched, printed>>

\* Submit a brand-new order into the open book.
Submit(o) ==
    /\ o \notin open
    /\ o \notin matched
    /\ o \notin printed
    /\ open' = open \cup {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, matched, printed>>

\* The token holder moves an open order into the matched book.
Match(o, t) ==
    /\ token = t
    /\ o \in open
    /\ open' = open \ {o}
    /\ matched' = matched \cup {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, printed>>

\* The token holder irreversibly prints a matched order, moving it into the terminal printed book.
Print(o, t) ==
    /\ token = t
    /\ o \in matched
    /\ matched' = matched \ {o}
    /\ printed' = printed \cup {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, open>>

\* Admin override: return a matched order to the open book.
Override(o) ==
    /\ o \in matched
    /\ matched' = matched \ {o}
    /\ open' = open \cup {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, printed>>

Next ==
    \/ Pass
    \/ \E o \in Orders : Submit(o) \/ Override(o)
    \/ \E o \in Orders, t \in Traders : Match(o, t) \/ Print(o, t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* At most once: the open, matched, and printed books are pairwise disjoint, so an order that
\* has been printed is in no other book and can never be matched and printed again.
BooksDisjoint ==
    /\ open \cap matched = {}
    /\ matched \cap printed = {}
    /\ open \cap printed = {}
====
nl:
A stock-exchange opening auction runs a single matching engine that only the trader currently
holding the ring token may operate. Each order lives in exactly one of three disjoint books:
open, matched, or printed. A brand-new order is submitted into the open book. The token holder
moves an open order into the matched book, and then irreversibly prints it -- moving it out of
matched and into the printed book, which is terminal. Because printing requires the order to be
sitting in the matched book and moves it out of matched, an order can be printed at most once. A
privileged admin may override a matched order, returning it to the open book. The ring token is
passed from trader to trader so that access to the matching engine stays exclusive.

Actions: pass the ring token to the next trader; submit a new order into the open book; the
token holder moves an open order into matched; the token holder irreversibly prints a matched
order into the terminal printed book; admin-override a matched order back to open.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the open, matched, and printed books are always pairwise disjoint, so an order
that has been printed sits in no other book and can never be matched and printed a second time.

---- MODULE W4Od18m6p4t3 ----
\* A smart-home door-lock network hands out control leases on devices, and at most a bounded
\* number of devices may be leased at once. A member acquires a device under a lease with an
\* expiry deadline while capacity allows, renews it before expiry, or loses it once the lease
\* expires. A slow member may let its lease lapse but is never treated as failed. An acquisition
\* attempted while at capacity is rejected (counted as backpressure). The lease clock keeps
\* ticking. The number of devices leased at once never exceeds the bound.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Devices == {0, 1, 2}
Capacity == 2
TTL == 2
MaxT == 2
MaxDenied == 3

VARIABLES leased, expiry, clock, denied

vars == <<leased, expiry, clock, denied>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ leased \in SUBSET Devices
    /\ expiry \in [Devices -> 0 .. TTL + MaxT]
    /\ clock \in 0 .. MaxT
    /\ denied \in 0 .. MaxDenied

Init ==
    /\ leased = {}
    /\ expiry = [d \in Devices |-> 0]
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ denied = 0

\* Acquire a device under a fresh lease while capacity allows.
Acquire(d) ==
    /\ d \notin leased
    /\ Cardinality(leased) < Capacity
    /\ leased' = leased \cup {d}
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![d] = clock + TTL]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, denied>>

\* Renew the lease on a held device.
Renew(d) ==
    /\ d \in leased
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![d] = clock + TTL]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leased, clock, denied>>

\* An expired lease releases the device.
Expire(d) ==
    /\ d \in leased
    /\ clock >= expiry[d]
    /\ leased' = leased \ {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<expiry, clock, denied>>

\* An acquisition attempted while at capacity is rejected as backpressure.
Reject ==
    /\ Cardinality(leased) = Capacity
    /\ denied < MaxDenied
    /\ denied' = denied + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leased, expiry, clock>>

\* The lease clock advances, cycling within a bounded band; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ clock' = (clock + 1) % (MaxT + 1)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leased, expiry, denied>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Devices : Acquire(d) \/ Renew(d) \/ Expire(d)
    \/ Reject
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounded capacity: the number of devices leased at once never exceeds the bound.
WithinLeaseCap == Cardinality(leased) <= Capacity
====
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network hands out control leases on its devices, and at most a bounded
number of devices may be leased at any one time. A household member acquires a device under a
lease with an expiry deadline, but only while the number of currently leased devices is below
the bound. A held lease may be renewed before it expires, and once a lease's deadline has passed
the device is released. A slow member may let its lease lapse rather than renewing promptly, but
it is never treated as failed. An acquisition attempted while the network is already at the
capacity bound is rejected and counted as backpressure. The lease clock advances continuously,
cycling within a bounded band.

Actions: acquire a device under a fresh lease while under the bound; renew a held lease; release
an expired lease; reject an acquisition attempted at capacity, counting backpressure; advance
the lease clock.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of devices leased at once never exceeds the fixed capacity bound.
