---- MODULE W4Od3m9p5t5 ----
\* A bank's interbank settlement batch settles items in numbered epochs. An item is admitted to
\* the current batch, then authorized -- arming a single settlement authorization for it.
\* Settling the item is the irreversible act: it fires and consumes that authorization, recording
\* the item as settled, so an item settles at most once. Reconfiguring to a new epoch clears the
\* batch admissions and all outstanding authorizations. A privileged admin may override, revoking
\* an armed authorization without settling.
EXTENDS Naturals

Items == {0, 1, 2}
MaxEpoch == 2

VARIABLES epoch, pending, authTok, settled

vars == <<epoch, pending, authTok, settled>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ pending \in SUBSET Items
    /\ authTok \in [Items -> {0, 1}]
    /\ settled \in SUBSET Items

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ authTok = [i \in Items |-> 0]
    /\ settled = {}

\* Reconfigure to the next epoch, clearing batch admissions and all authorizations.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch' = (epoch + 1) % (MaxEpoch + 1)
    /\ pending' = {}
    /\ authTok' = [i \in Items |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED settled

\* Admit an unsettled item into the current batch.
Admit(i) ==
    /\ i \notin settled
    /\ i \notin pending
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {i}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, authTok, settled>>

\* Authorize an admitted, unsettled item, arming its settlement authorization.
Authorize(i) ==
    /\ i \in pending
    /\ i \notin settled
    /\ authTok[i] = 0
    /\ authTok' = [authTok EXCEPT ![i] = 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, pending, settled>>

\* The irreversible settlement: fire and consume the authorization, recording the item settled.
Settle(i) ==
    /\ authTok[i] = 1
    /\ i \notin settled
    /\ authTok' = [authTok EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
    /\ settled' = settled \cup {i}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, pending>>

\* Admin override: revoke an armed authorization without settling.
Override(i) ==
    /\ authTok[i] = 1
    /\ authTok' = [authTok EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, pending, settled>>

Next ==
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E i \in Items : Admit(i) \/ Authorize(i) \/ Settle(i) \/ Override(i)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* At most once: any settled item has a consumed authorization, so its irreversible settlement
\* can never fire a second time.
SettleOnce == \A i \in Items : i \in settled => authTok[i] = 0
====
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch settles items in numbered epochs. An item is first admitted
into the current batch. An admitted, unsettled item may then be authorized, which arms a single
settlement authorization for it. Settling the item is the irreversible act: it fires and consumes
that authorization, and records the item as settled, so an item can settle at most once.
Reconfiguring to the next epoch clears all batch admissions and every outstanding authorization,
though items already settled stay settled. A privileged admin may override at any time, revoking
an armed authorization without settling the item.

Actions: reconfigure to the next epoch, clearing admissions and authorizations; admit an unsettled
item into the current batch; authorize an admitted unsettled item, arming its authorization;
irreversibly settle an authorized item, consuming the authorization and recording it settled;
admin-override to revoke an armed authorization without settling.

SAFETY PROPERTY: any item that has been settled has a consumed settlement authorization, so the
irreversible settlement of an item can never fire a second time.

---- MODULE W4Od11m5p5t2 ----
\* A print-shop job spooler runs two independent instances that share one job pool. A job is
\* submitted to the pool, then approved by voters. Printing a job -- the irreversible act -- is
\* allowed only once a strict majority has approved it; printing consumes that quorum (clearing
\* the job's votes) and removes the job from the shared pool. Because printing clears the votes
\* and pulls the job from the pool, the two instances cannot both print the same job: a job is
\* printed at most once.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Jobs == {0, 1}
Voters == {0, 1, 2}
Inst == {"A", "B"}

VARIABLES pool, votes, printed, turn

vars == <<pool, votes, printed, turn>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ pool \in SUBSET Jobs
    /\ votes \in [Jobs -> SUBSET Voters]
    /\ printed \in SUBSET Jobs
    /\ turn \in Inst

Init ==
    /\ pool = {}
    /\ votes = [j \in Jobs |-> {}]
    /\ printed = {}
    /\ turn = "A"

\* Submit a fresh, never-printed job into the shared pool.
Submit(j) ==
    /\ j \notin pool
    /\ j \notin printed
    /\ pool' = pool \cup {j}
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![j] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<printed, turn>>

\* A voter approves a pooled job.
Approve(j, v) ==
    /\ j \in pool
    /\ v \notin votes[j]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![j] = votes[j] \cup {v}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, printed, turn>>

\* An instance prints a job with a strict-majority quorum: consuming the quorum, marking it
\* printed, and pulling it from the shared pool.
Print(i, j) ==
    /\ j \in pool
    /\ j \notin printed
    /\ 2 * Cardinality(votes[j]) > Cardinality(Voters)
    /\ printed' = printed \cup {j}
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![j] = {}]
    /\ pool' = pool \ {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED turn

\* The two instances take turns polling the shared pool; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ turn' = IF turn = "A" THEN "B" ELSE "A"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, votes, printed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Submit(j)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs, v \in Voters : Approve(j, v)
    \/ \E i \in Inst, j \in Jobs : Print(i, j)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* At most once: any printed job has no standing quorum, so neither instance can print it again.
PrintOnce == \A j \in Jobs : j \in printed => votes[j] = {}
====
nl:
A print-shop job spooler runs two independent spooler instances that share one job pool. A job
is first submitted into the shared pool, where it starts with no approvals. Voters then approve a
pooled job. Printing a job is the irreversible act, and an instance may print a job only once a
strict majority of voters has approved it. Printing consumes that quorum -- clearing the job's
votes -- marks the job as printed, and removes it from the shared pool. Because printing both
clears the votes and pulls the job out of the shared pool, the two instances can never both print
the same job. The two instances take turns polling the shared pool throughout.

Actions: submit a fresh job into the shared pool; a voter approves a pooled job; an instance
prints a job that has a strict-majority quorum, consuming the quorum, marking it printed, and
removing it from the pool; alternate the polling turn between the two instances.

SAFETY PROPERTY: any job that has been printed has no standing quorum of votes, so neither
instance can ever print the same job a second time.
